recipe.title: Garlic-Ginger Chicken Thighs with Broccoli and Soy Glaze
recipe.description: Tender chicken thighs braised with garlic, ginger and soy sauce, served with crisp‑tender broccoli – a quick, comforting dish inspired by Chinese home cooking.

Season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper, then toss the steamed broccoli into the pan to coat with sauce.

recipe.title: Soy‑Egg Fried Rice with Ginger‑Garlic Broccoli
recipe.description: A classic wok‑fried rice that turns raw rice into a fragrant, satisfying dinner, enriched with eggs, broccoli, and a ginger‑garlic soy sauce.
instructions: Rinse the 300 g of rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
Add the rinsed rice and 600 ml of water to a saucepan; bring to a boil over medium heat.
Once boiling, reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove the saucepan from the heat, let the rice sit, covered, for 3 minutes, then fluff with a fork and spread on a tray to cool slightly (this prevents clumping).
Cut the broccoli into small florets.
Blanch the broccoli florets in boiling water for 3 minutes; drain and set aside.
Peel and mince the 2 garlic cloves; grate the 1 tsp of ginger.
Beat the 2 eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger; stir‑fry for 20 seconds until aromatic.
Push the aromatics to the side and pour in the beaten eggs; scramble quickly for 1 minute, breaking into soft ribbons.
Add the cooked rice, spreading it evenly; stir‑fry for 3 minutes, allowing the rice to heat through and develop light browning.
Stir in the blanched broccoli, then drizzle 3 tbsp soy sauce; mix well and cook for 2 more minutes.
Season with 1 pinch pepper, taste and adjust with an extra pinch of salt if needed.
Slice the spring onion stalks thinly and toss into the rice just before serving.
tips: Using freshly cooked rice that has been cooled slightly yields a softer texture than day‑old rice and still prevents sogginess.
For extra umami, add a splash of the cooking liquid from the chicken‑thighs (if prepared separately) after the soy sauce.

recipe.title: Steamed Egg Custard with Ginger‑Soy broth (Japanese‑style Tamago Jiru)
recipe.description: A light, silky egg custard soup flavored with ginger, garlic, and soy sauce, served with a side of steamed broccoli – perfect for a gentle evening meal.
instructions: Bring 400 ml water to a gentle boil in a saucepan; add 1 tsp vegetable oil to reduce foaming.
Peel and finely mince the garlic clove; grate the 1 tsp ginger.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the boiling water; simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 pinch salt; keep the broth at a low simmer.
In a bowl, beat the 4 eggs until uniform.
Very slowly pour the hot broth into the beaten eggs while whisking constantly (tempering) to avoid curdling.
Return the egg‑broth mixture to the saucepan, lower the heat to low, and cover.
Simmer gently for 12 minutes; the custard should set but still wobble slightly when the pan is shaken.
While the custard cooks, cut the broccoli into small florets and steam over boiling water for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Check the custard: the surface should be smooth and the center should be firm enough to hold a spoon.
Divide the steamed broccoli between two bowls, pour the hot egg custard over the broccoli, and garnish with thinly sliced spring onion stalks.
tips: Do not let the broth boil vigorously after adding the eggs, or the custard will become grainy.
For a richer flavor, replace half of the water with low‑sodium chicken broth if available.

recipe.title: Mediterranean Stuffed Aubergine with Chickpeas and Spinach
recipe.description: Roasted aubergine halves filled with a savory mixture of chickpeas, spinach, tomatoes, and lemon‑tahini sauce, inspired by Turkish and Greek flavors.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Slice each aubergine in half lengthwise and scoop out a shallow cavity, leaving about 1 cm of flesh attached to the skin.
Brush the cut sides with 1 tbsp olive oil, season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper, and place cut‑side up on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the flesh is tender and the edges are lightly browned.
While the aubergine roasts, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 tsp ground cumin; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the canned chickpeas (400 g), drained and rinsed, the chopped tomatoes (2 pieces), and the spinach; cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the spinach wilts and the tomatoes soften.
Season the mixture with the remaining 1 pinch salt, 1 pinch black pepper, and the juice of half the lemon; stir well.
Remove the roasted aubergine halves from the oven; fill each cavity with the chickpea‑spinach mixture.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tbsp tahini, the juice of the remaining half lemon, and 2 tbsp water until smooth; drizzle the sauce over the stuffed aubergines.
Return to the oven for another 5 minutes to let flavors meld, then serve hot.
tips: If the aubergine flesh is very watery, sprinkle a little extra salt on the cut side and let it sit 10 minutes before roasting; pat dry with paper towels.
Add a pinch of smoked paprika to the filling for a subtle smoky note.

recipe.title: Spicy Plantain & Black‑Eyed Bean Breakfast Stew
recipe.description: A hearty, one‑pot stew that turns urgent ripe plantains and pantry beans into a warming morning dish, flavored with tomato and onion.
instructions: Peel the 2 plantains, slice them into 1‑cm thick rounds.
Dice the onion and the 2 tomatoes.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a medium pot over medium heat; add the onion and sauté 3 minutes, until translucent.
Add the plantain rounds, sprinkle 1 tsp paprika, 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper, and fry 4 minutes, turning once, until the edges turn golden.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and cook 2 minutes, until they soften and release juices.

Add the 200 g black‑eyed beans (pre‑rinsed if canned) and 150 ml water; bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer on low heat for 10 minutes, until the plantains are tender and the sauce thickens.
Crack the 2 eggs directly into the pot, cover, and poach for 3 minutes, until whites are set and yolks are still runny.
Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt or pepper if needed.
Serve the stew hot, spooning the poached eggs over each bowl.
tips: If the beans are dry, soak them overnight and cook them 45 minutes beforehand; otherwise use canned beans for speed.
For extra heat, add a finely chopped green chili with the onion.
The dish can be enjoyed with a slice of crusty bread on the side.

Mientras tanto, recalienta el cuscús sobrante en una olla a fuego bajo, removiendo, hasta que esté humeante en el centro (aprox. 3 minutos).
Sirve el tagine sobre una cama de cuscús rehidratado, decorando con un chorrito de aceite de oliva y cilantro opcional.

recipe.title: Harira ligera con cuscús y huevo pochado
recipe.description: Una versión rápida de la tradicional sopa harira marroquí, usando cuscús sobrante como espesante y un huevo pochado para darle cuerpo, ideal para una cena ligera.
instructions: Escurre y enjuaga los garbanzos; reserva.
Pica la cebolla, el pimiento rojo y la zanahoria en cubos pequeños.
En una olla grande a fuego medio, calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva y sofríe la cebolla 4 minutos, hasta que esté transparente.
Añade la zanahoria y el pimiento; cocina 3 minutos más.
Incorpora el cordero picado y el comino; cocina 5 minutos, removiendo, hasta que la carne pierda el tono rosado y alcance 63 °C en el centro (jugos claros).
Vierte el tomate triturado, los garbanzos y 800 ml de agua; lleva a ebullición.
Reduce a fuego bajo y cocina 12 minutos, removiendo ocasionalmente, hasta que la sopa adquiera cuerpo.
Recalienta el cuscús sobrante en una cacerola a fuego bajo, removiendo, hasta que esté humeante en el centro (aprox. 3 minutos).
Añade el cuscús al caldo y mezcla bien.

Para los huevos pochados: lleva a ebullición 1 l de agua con una pizca de vinagre, reduce a fuego bajo y crea un remolino con una cuchara. Desliza un huevo y cocina 3 minutos, hasta que la clara esté firme y la yema líquida. Repite con los 3 huevos.
Sirve la harira en cuencos hondos, coloca un huevo pochado encima de cada porción y espolvorea cilantro picado, sal y pimienta al gusto.
tips: Si prefieres una sopa más espesa, tritura una parte de los garbanzos con una cuchara antes de añadir el cuscús.
El huevo pochado aporta proteína y hace la sopa más saciante sin añadir grasa.

recipe.title: Pork Tenderloin with Dijon‑Cream Sauce and Sautéed Green Beans
recipe.description: A tender pork roast glazed with a tangy Dijon‑cream sauce, served with crisp green beans tossed in shallots and melted Gruyère.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry, season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an oven‑proof skillet over medium heat; sear the pork on all sides, about 2 minutes per side, until golden.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast for 15‑18 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 63 °C and the meat is tender; let rest 5 minutes before slicing.
While the pork roasts, trim the green beans and remove the ends.
Slice the shallots thinly.
In a second pan, heat 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat; add the shallots and sauté 3 minutes, until softened and fragrant.
Add the green beans, season with a pinch of salt, and stir‑fry 5‑6 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Stir in 30 ml cream and the remaining 1 tbsp Dijon mustard; cook 2 minutes, until the sauce coats the beans.
Remove the pan from heat and sprinkle the grated Gruyère over the beans; cover briefly to melt.
Slice the rested pork into 1‑cm medallions.
Serve the pork medallions drizzled with the remaining pan juices, alongside the creamy green beans.
tips: If the pork looks slightly pink after 63 °C, let it rest; residual heat will finish cooking.
For extra flavor, deglaze the pork pan with a splash of water before adding the mustard‑cream sauce.

recipe.title: Leek and Shallot Velouté with a Gruyère Crumble
recipe.description: Silky pureed leeks and shallots, brightened with a touch of cream and finished with a crunchy Gruyère crumble – a light starter perfect for a French‑style dinner.
instructions: Trim the dark green parts off the leeks, slice the white and light green sections thinly, then rinse under cold water.
Peel and finely dice the shallots.
Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat; add the leeks and shallots, sauté 5 minutes, until softened but not browned.
Add 600 ml water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer; cook 12 minutes, until the leeks are completely tender.
Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Using an immersion blender, puree the vegetables until smooth; return to low heat.
Stir in the cream and warm for 2 minutes, just to integrate.
While the soup simmers, grate the Gruyère and spread it on a small baking sheet.
Place the sheet under a hot broiler for 2‑3 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese turns golden and crisp; let cool, then break into coarse crumbs.
Ladle the velouté into bowls and sprinkle each with a generous handful of Gruyère crumble.
tips: For an extra aromatic note, add a tiny pinch of nutmeg to the soup just before serving.
If you prefer a smoother texture, pass the blended soup through a fine sieve.

recipe.title: Pan‑Seared Pork Tenderloin Medallions with Mustard‑Green Bean Ragout
recipe.description: Thin pork medallions quickly pan‑seared and finished in a mustard‑flavored ragout of green beans, leeks, and shallots – a fast, hearty main that stays light.
instructions: Slice the pork tenderloin into 1‑cm thick medallions; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Trim the green beans, cutting them into 4‑cm pieces.
Clean the leek, slice the white part thinly.
Peel and finely mince the shallots.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat; add the pork medallions and sear 2‑3 minutes per side, until a golden crust forms and the interior reaches 63 °C. Transfer the pork to a plate and keep warm.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil; lower to medium heat and add the shallots and leeks, sauté 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the green beans, season with a pinch of salt, and stir‑fry 5 minutes, until they begin to soften but retain crunch.
Stir in the Dijon mustard and cream; cook 2 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and coat the vegetables.
Return the pork medallions to the pan, nestle them into the ragout, and heat together 1 minute just to re‑warm the meat.
Serve each plate with two medallions atop a generous spoonful of the mustard‑green bean ragout.
tips: Do not overcrowd the pan when searing the pork; work in batches if necessary to keep the heat high.
If the sauce becomes too thick, add a splash of water to reach the desired consistency.
